# Implemented services and features

TinyStack implements **64 service APIs** with **1,582 selected operations**.

This catalogue records the capabilities available in the current checkout. Each service implements a subset;
its reference documents supported operations, inputs, and behavior limits. Execution modes show when a
feature manages records or needs a Docker runtime.

## Shared platform features

| Feature | Implemented behavior | Reference |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Fault injection | Ordered gateway rules inject protocol-correct AWS errors and cancellable latency by service, operation, Region and account, with probability, startup configuration, reset restoration, diagnostics and LocalStack Chaos API aliases. | [Details](../guides/fault-injection.md) |
| AWS wire protocols | AWS JSON 1.0/1.1, AWS Query, EC2 Query, REST XML/JSON, and Smithy RPC v2 CBOR through generated bindings. | [Details](../architecture/request-flow.md) |
| Identity and resource scope | Configured access-key accounts, IAM/STS credential lookup, regional and account-wide scopes, and optional SigV4 verification; general IAM permission evaluation is outside the subset. | [Details](../architecture/identity.md) |
| Transactional storage and persistence | Atomic callback transactions, in-memory storage, and optional SQLite commit persistence with resource reload on restart; runtime and in-flight state have separate limits. | [Details](../guides/persistence.md) |
| Cloudscape console | AWS-style dark dashboard with configurable widgets, a favorites bar of starred services, visit history, categorized service catalog with AWS icons, shared top-bar account/Region menus, resource inventory/details, IAM, S3, SQS, SNS, Lambda, DynamoDB, EventBridge, CloudWatch Logs and CloudWatch metrics/alarms/dashboard, API Gateway HTTP/REST, Step Functions, and EC2/VPC management workflows, recent requests, delivery history, and metrics through a separately served web console. | [Details](../guides/diagnostics.md) |
| Diagnostics | Health/resource endpoints, bounded request and delivery logs, model-sensitive body redaction, and Prometheus request metrics. | [Details](../guides/diagnostics.md) |
| Init hooks and reset | LocalStack-style boot, start, ready and shutdown scripts (also read from /etc/localstack/init) with a status endpoint, and a POST reset endpoint that clears all stored state and can re-run the ready scripts. | [Details](../guides/init-hooks.md) |
| CLI and SDK clients | Local endpoint overrides for AWS clients, CLI wrappers, and generated Go SDK-compatible APIs. | [Details](../getting-started/clients.md) |
| Infrastructure workflows | Selected Terraform AWS provider workflows and local CloudFormation/SAM deployment through the registered resource-type subset. | [Details](../guides/infrastructure.md) |
| Runtime adapters | Docker Lambda execution and opt-in ECS Docker tasks, EKS k3s clusters, and ElastiCache Docker nodes; default optional adapters manage records. | [Details](../guides/runtimes.md) |
| Cross-service event delivery | Supported notification, rule, and event-source workflows connect local service implementations and record delivery outcomes. | [Details](../guides/events.md) |

## Service features

Use the [support matrix](index.md) to compare operation counts and execution modes.

### Analytics

#### Amazon MSK

Store provisioned Standard cluster configuration, monitoring settings and tags without a Kafka runtime.

**Execution:** Configuration records only. **Selected operations:** 8.

- Eight pinned Kafka REST JSON operations: CreateCluster, DescribeCluster, ListClusters, DeleteCluster, UpdateMonitoring, ListTagsForResource, TagResource and UntagResource.
- Commercial account/Region/name/UUID cluster ARNs, scoped name uniqueness, creation timestamp, deeply retained broker/network/EBS/version/monitoring metadata and opaque optimistic configuration revisions.
- Finite creation matrix: explicit Kafka 3.8.x/3.9.x and kafka.m5.large/xlarge, us-east-1/us-west-1/us-west-2, 2-3 scoped EC2 subnets in distinct AZs (exactly 2 in us-west-1), nodes evenly distributed, explicit security groups and EBS volume size.
- Atomic monitoring CAS, optional delete CAS, tag merges/removals with MSK limits, scope/API/filter-bound deterministic list cursors that survive cursor deletion.
- CloudFormation AWS::MSK::Cluster Ref/GetAtt Arn and CurrentVersion, owned/external tags plus monitoring in one write, actual live-state compensation with fresh revisions, safe create-first immutable replacement and collision rollback.
- SQLite restart, offline archive export/import and reset use the existing storage lifecycle; inventory reports RecordsOnly=true and ExecutionReady=false; real RGTA tag operations, official icon and Terraform kafka endpoint key.

[Supported operations](kafka.md#supported-operations) · [Limitations](kafka.md#limitations-and-future-work)

#### Athena

Query local S3 data through the Glue catalog using an in-memory SQLite SQL engine.

**Execution:** SQLite SQL engine. **Selected operations:** 25.

- Workgroups, named queries, query execution metadata, pagination and client tokens.
- SELECT queries over CSV, delimited text and JSON, including gzip data.
- Glue catalog DDL, SHOW, DESCRIBE, MSCK REPAIR and partition changes.
- Query results are retained and written to the configured S3 output location.

[Supported operations](athena.md#supported-operations) · [Limitations](athena.md#limitations-and-future-work)

#### Glue Data Catalog

Create the databases, tables, and partitions that local Athena queries use.

**Execution:** Local behavior. **Selected operations:** 19.

- Database CRUD, tags and pagination.
- Table CRUD and batch deletion.
- Partition CRUD, batch operations and partition listings.
- Names are normalized to lowercase; deleting a database removes its tables and partitions.

[Supported operations](glue.md#supported-operations) · [Limitations](glue.md#limitations-and-future-work)

### Application Integration

#### Amazon MQ

Store scoped broker configuration and tags without provisioning brokers or running a messaging engine.

**Execution:** Records only. **Selected operations:** 8.

- Eight pinned REST JSON broker/tag APIs: CreateBroker, DescribeBroker, ListBrokers, UpdateBroker, DeleteBroker, CreateTags, ListTags and DeleteTags.
- Stable commercial scoped broker IDs/ARNs and creation metadata; exact SQLite restart and offline fixture export/import, with shared reset of broker and idempotency records.
- Finite ActiveMQ 5.18/5.19 micro/large and RabbitMQ 3.13 mq.m5.large creation combinations; engine-specific deployment and RabbitMQ micro-downgrade restrictions; validated initial write-only credentials with only username metadata retained.
- Explicit private EC2 subnet/security-group metadata lookup with scoped existence, counts, one VPC and distinct Availability Zones; no network allocation.
- Persistent scoped creator-token replay/conflict semantics, atomic name uniqueness and effective-candidate updates; retained false log/public flags and documented maintenance/encryption defaults.
- Atomic merged tags, ARN-scoped tag APIs and Resource Groups Tagging API integration; deterministic 20-default/5-100-bound pages with scope/API-bound deletion-resilient cursors.
- CloudFormation AWS::AmazonMQ::Broker Ref ID/GetAtt Arn, owned/external tags and configuration in one atomic update, live-state rollback and create-first replacement with collision preservation.
- Resource browser RecordsOnly=true/ExecutionReady=false, official AWS icon and actual Terraform mq endpoint key.

[Supported operations](mq.md#supported-operations) · [Limitations](mq.md#limitations-and-future-work)

### Compute and containers

#### AWS Batch

Persist regional compute-environment, queue and revisioned container-definition metadata without provisioning or running jobs.

**Execution:** Records only. **Selected operations:** 14.

- 14 REST JSON metadata operations: compute environment and queue CRUD, definition registration/description/deregistration and resource tags.
- UNMANAGED and finite x86 MANAGED EC2 records must be created ENABLED (omitted state defaults to ENABLED); explicit DISABLED creation returns ClientException/400 without storing a record. Updates accept ENABLED/DISABLED; VALID describes local metadata, with no fabricated ECS cluster or runtime identifiers.
- Managed capacity/configuration retains vCPU bounds, desired capacity, instance choices, instance profile and actual scoped EC2 subnet/security-group references; all network lookups share the storage transaction.
- Queues retain normalized ordered compute-environment ARNs, priority and state; create requires 1-3 associations, update can disassociate all. Referenced or enabled environments cannot be deleted; queues must also be disabled before deletion.
- Job definitions preserve monotonically increasing scoped revisions and revisioned ARNs, active/inactive history, container image/command, legacy CPU/memory or VCPU/MEMORY requirements, environment, role and parameter metadata.
- Atomic writes and failed mutations, account/Region isolation, deterministic filter-bound pagination and concurrent registration/name uniqueness.
- Tags are scoped to each resource ARN and definition revision, with 50-key merge limits, inventory and Resource Groups Tagging API support.
- SQLite restart, offline fixture export/import into a fresh store followed by normal restart, shared reset, verified SigV4, official console icon and Terraform batch endpoint.
- CloudFormation ComputeEnvironment, JobQueue and JobDefinition selected properties with correct ARN Ref/GetAtt, queue dependency updates, definition revision replacement and original-incarnation rollback. Removed template tags free capacity before additions; failed additions compensate live removed values.

[Supported operations](batch.md#supported-operations) · [Limitations](batch.md#limitations-and-future-work)

### Configuration and operations

#### Cloud Control API

Manage live S3 buckets and SQS queues with the CloudFormation resource handlers and a durable request journal.

**Execution:** Local behavior. **Selected operations:** 7.

- CreateResource, GetResource, UpdateResource, DeleteResource and ListResources for AWS::S3::Bucket and AWS::SQS::Queue.
- BucketName, Tags and VersioningConfiguration.Status (Enabled or Suspended) for buckets; queue names, FIFO settings, supported queue attributes and tags for queues.
- Generated resource names when omitted; identifiers are bucket names or queue URLs, as in the resource schemas.
- Reads live state from S3 and SQS, including resources created directly or through CloudFormation; lists identifiers with pagination.
- RFC 6902 JSON Patch updates with add, remove, replace, move, copy and test; create-only and read-only changes fail explicitly.
- Synchronous writes return SUCCESS or FAILED ProgressEvents with modeled handler error codes and request tokens.
- GetResourceRequestStatus and paginated ListResourceRequests with operation and status filters; request history is account/Region scoped and visible for seven days.
- ClientToken replays the original progress event for 36 hours and rejects conflicting requests; concurrent writes to the same resource are rejected.
- Request history and client tokens survive persistent restart; interrupted writes become FAILED and release resource locks.
- Created resources appear under S3 or SQS in the console inventory, Resource Groups and Tagging API; Cloud Control creates no separate resource copies.

[Supported operations](cloudcontrol.md#supported-operations) · [Limitations](cloudcontrol.md#limitations-and-future-work)

#### Resource Groups

Group resources with tag-based or CloudFormation stack queries, resolved against the same resources the Tagging API lists.

#### WAF v2

Persist scoped web ACLs, IP sets, rule groups, tags and regional association metadata without inspecting traffic.

**Execution:** Records only. **Selected operations:** 22.

- 22 AWS JSON 1.1 operations for Create/Get/Update/Delete/ListWebACL, IPSet and RuleGroup, four regional association APIs and three tag APIs; SDK signing name wafv2 and target prefix AWSWAF_20190729 come from the pinned Smithy model.
- Stable names, UUIDs, resource ARNs and internal creation timestamps; descriptions, Allow/Block DefaultAction, VisibilityConfig booleans and metric names, declared immutable RuleGroup Capacity and selected Rules persist atomically.
- REGIONAL records are isolated by account and Region; CLOUDFRONT records use us-east-1 and global ARN paths, with separate name namespaces and pagination cursors.
- Rules support only direct IPSetReferenceStatement in ACLs/groups and RuleGroupReferenceStatement in ACLs; exact existing same-account/Region/scope references, unique names/priorities and required visibility configuration.
- Direct IP references select exactly one Allow, Block or Count Action; ACL rule-group references select exactly one None or Count OverrideAction without Action; these are configuration records only.
- IPV4 and IPV6 CIDRs, including individual /32 and /128 addresses, empty address arrays and all nonzero prefix lengths; at most 10000 addresses, with atomic family/range validation and immutable family.
- Get/List/Create return current configuration LockToken; Update/Delete compare tokens and write/rotate in one serializable store transaction, with exactly one concurrent winner for a shared old token; tokens survive SQLite restart and tag/association changes.
- Association replacement, idempotent disassociation, empty GetWebACLForResource when unassociated and sorted ListResourcesForWebACL; default APPLICATION_LOAD_BALANCER or explicit API_GATEWAY filters.
- Creation tags, atomic TagResource/UntagResource, validated unique keys and 50-tag limit; deterministic tag pagination; generic inventory, Resource Groups Tagging API, official WAF console catalogue icon and Terraform wafv2 endpoint.
- List and tag pagination use Limit 1-100 and cursors bound to account, Region, operation and WAF scope or ARN; resources sort by name/UUID and tags by key, with resume after deletion.
- CloudFormation AWS::WAFv2::WebACL, IPSet, RuleGroup and WebACLAssociation selected properties; name|id|scope Ref, Arn/Id GetAtt on configuration resources, live lock-token fetch for update/delete, tag replacement at 50 tags, compensation and stack rollback; shared reset clears all WAF records.

[Supported operations](wafv2.md#supported-operations) · [Limitations](wafv2.md#limitations-and-future-work)

#### AWS Account

- GetRegionOptStatus validates RegionName against the 28-region commercial subset and returns the opt-in status including configured per-account overrides.

#### AWS Backup

Persist regional vaults, immutable backup-plan versions and resource-selection metadata without running backups.

**Execution:** Records only. **Selected operations:** 17.

- 17 REST JSON operations for vault CRUD, plan CRUD and version listing, resource-selection CRUD and vault/plan tags.
- Vault names, stable ARNs and millisecond creation dates; optional same-account/Region KMS key ARN metadata (UUID or multi-Region key ID, not aliases); recovery-point count is always zero.
- Named plans with 1-10 unique named rules, existing regional target vaults, supported UTC cron expressions, start/completion windows, cold-storage and deletion lifecycle days, and up to 10 RecoveryPointTags per rule.
- Each update creates an immutable version with a new version ID and creation timestamp; plan IDs/ARNs remain stable and rule IDs are retained for unchanged rule names; exact VersionId retrieval and version pagination.
- Selections store names, role ARNs, up to 500 unique explicit commercial resource ARNs without wildcards and up to 30 unique STRINGEQUALS tag selectors; explicit resources and selectors can coexist as metadata.
- Selection IDs are distinct even when display names repeat; at most 100 selections and 10 tag-based selections per plan; plan deletion requires removing selections first.
- Deleting a plan removes the current version from GetBackupPlan while preserving older version retrieval; ListBackupPlans IncludeDeleted and version lists retain deletion metadata.
- Regional CreatorRequestId replay for vaults/plans and per-plan replay for selections returns the original creation identity without overwriting records; token/name checks and writes are atomic.
- Creation tags and atomic TagResource/UntagResource on vaults/plans with shared tag validation and 50-tag limit; paginated ListTags and Resource Groups Tagging API integration.
- Deterministic ID/name sorting, MaxResults 1-1000, resume-after-deletion cursors bound to account, Region, operation and filter/parent; vault-type/shared and IncludeDeleted filters.
- Account/Region isolation, SQLite restart and shared reset; generic inventory, official console catalogue icon and Terraform backup endpoint.
- CloudFormation BackupVault, BackupPlan and BackupSelection selected properties, stable Ref/GetAtt, plan and tag updates, selection replacement, rollback and deletion.

### Storage

#### Amazon EFS

Persist regional file-system, mount-target and access-point metadata without a mountable NFS filesystem.

**Execution:** Records only. **Selected operations:** 15.

- 15 REST JSON operations for file-system CRUD, mount-target CRUD/security-group replacement, access-point CRUD and resource tags; SDK signing name elasticfilesystem from the pinned model.
- Stable fs/fsmt/fsap IDs, filesystem/access-point ARNs, creation tokens, account/Region ownership, encryption/KMS metadata, performance and throughput configuration, POSIX user/root metadata and creation tags.
- FileSystemAlreadyExists and AccessPointAlreadyExists return original identifiers on token reuse without mutating initial records, including conflicting retries; tokens are scoped to account/Region and removed with records.
- Locally available metadata defaults: generalPurpose performance, bursting throughput, Encrypted=false, zero size/usage values and a fixed creation-time size timestamp. Mount-target count reflects stored records; no real data storage is represented.
- Atomic throughput updates with bursting/provisioned/elastic modes, provisioned 1-3414 MiBps including fractions; maxIO cannot use elastic. Identity, immutable settings and previous state survive failed updates.
- Existing scoped EC2 subnet/group lookup in the same transaction; no default VPC seeding or EC2 changes. One VPC per filesystem and one target per local AZ; IPv4 CIDR validation and deterministic unused EFS metadata addresses; at most five unique groups.
- Access points persist UID/GID, up to 16 secondary groups and optional root path/creation owner/mode settings. IDs are 0-4294967295, paths at most four non-dot-prefixed components and 100 Unicode characters; modes 3-4 octal digits.
- Filesystem/access-point references accept IDs or same-account/Region commercial ARNs; mount targets accept IDs only. Both mount targets and access points must be deleted before their filesystem; dependency errors preserve all state.
- Validated unique tags, modeled lengths/character sets/reserved prefixes and 50-tag limit; deterministic sorted retrieval, inventory and Resource Groups Tagging API filters elasticfilesystem:file-system/access-point.
- Scoped/filter-bound deterministic pagination with default 100 and positive requested sizes capped at 1000; stable ID/key order and resume after cursor deletion.
- SQLite restart, offline export/import fixtures and shared reset retain exact identifiers/configuration/relations/tokens; default app assembly, verified SigV4, resource browser, official console icon and Terraform efs endpoint.
- CloudFormation FileSystem/MountTarget/AccessPoint Ref/GetAtt, mutable throughput/security-group/tag updates and immutable replacement. EFS-specific retirement orders children first and restores original incarnations during rollback; 50-tag replacement and failed-tag compensation preserve unrelated tags.

[Supported operations](efs.md#supported-operations) · [Limitations](efs.md#limitations-and-future-work)

Send and verify email with the classic SES Query API over the same state as SES v2.

**Execution:** Recorded delivery. **Selected operations:** 23.

- Same signing name as SES v2: form requests reach v1 and REST JSON requests reach v2.
- VerifyEmailIdentity, VerifyEmailAddress, VerifyDomainIdentity and VerifyDomainDkim verify immediately, with three DKIM tokens for a domain.
- ListIdentities, GetIdentityVerificationAttributes, ListVerifiedEmailAddresses and DeleteIdentity read and write the identities SES v2 stores.
- SendEmail, SendRawEmail (MIME parsed with net/mail), SendTemplatedEmail and SendBulkTemplatedEmail check the sender, render templates, and record messages in the delivery log.
- CreateTemplate, GetTemplate, UpdateTemplate, DeleteTemplate and ListTemplates share SES v2 templates.
- CreateConfigurationSet, DeleteConfigurationSet, ListConfigurationSets and DescribeConfigurationSet share SES v2 configuration sets, whose events a send publishes.
- GetSendQuota and GetSendStatistics report the hourly send counts SES v2 keeps.

[Supported operations](ses.md#supported-operations) · [Limitations](ses.md#limitations-and-future-work)

#### SES v2

Render and inspect email workflows without sending external mail.

**Execution:** Recorded delivery. **Selected operations:** 24.

- Identities are verified immediately; templates and configuration sets are stored.
- SendEmail and bulk email validate senders and render a Handlebars subset.
- Delivery records contain messages; configuration set events reach SNS, EventBridge and Firehose.
- Mailbox simulator addresses generate bounce/complaint behavior.
- Identities, templates, configuration sets and send counts are shared with SES v1.

[Supported operations](sesv2.md#supported-operations) · [Limitations](sesv2.md#limitations-and-future-work)

#### Step Functions

Execute a local Amazon States Language subset with service integrations.

**Execution:** Local behavior. **Selected operations:** 34.

- State machines, versions, aliases, activities, executions and history.
- JSONPath and JSONata evaluation, supported state types, Retry/Catch and callbacks.
- In-process AWS SDK integrations can call implemented operations.
- TestState and redrive support.
- AWS-style console for scoped state machine creation, ASL validation and editing, execution roles, logging configuration and tags.
- Console starts and stops Standard executions with paginated execution history, input, output and failure details; Express workflows return synchronous results.

[Supported operations](sfn.md#supported-operations) · [Limitations](sfn.md#limitations-and-future-work)

## Keep the catalogue current

Feature descriptions live in `docs/catalog.json`; operation counts come from registered profiles.
Update the catalogue with each delivered service or feature, then run `task docs:generate` and
`task docs:check`. CI rejects stale generated pages and undocumented registered services.

See the [documentation workflow](../development/documentation.md) for maintenance.
Proposed additions remain in the [future catalogue](../roadmap/catalogue.md).
